subject: Private deployment: credential model & operator access (DPA questions)
messages:
From: Samantha Keller <samantha.keller@asterbio.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Mar 2028 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment: credential model & operator access (DPA questions)

Hi Aditya,

Thanks again for the demo last week. AsterBio's legal and security teams reviewed the initial DPA and a few open items came up specific to our private deployment requirements (VPC/on-prem styles). I attached our redlines (AsterBio-DPA-redlines-v1.pdf). High level asks: 

- Customer-controlled keys: we need a clear commitment that Redwood operators will not have the ability to export or derive customer master keys (CMKs) used to encrypt inference traffic or persisted artifacts.
- Support model: for break-glass support please describe the exact mechanism you propose for ephemeral operator sessions without key exposure.
- Subprocessors & transfers: call out subprocessors that will see metadata/telemetry; we need assurance about cross-border transfers and that no unredacted user content leaves our VPC.
- Evidence: SOC2/ISO evidence and a sample of the logs we would be allowed to review (redacted).

Can we get a short write-up from you covering: (1) credential separation approach for private deploys, (2) what operator telemetry looks like, and (3) a proposed limited subprocessor list for a transferless model? Procurement also asked for an estimated timeline to finalize this so they can start the PO.

Would love to schedule a 30m call if helpful — legal wants to sign something succinct by 2028-03-22.

Thanks,

Samantha Keller
Head of IT 
AsterBio

Attachments: AsterBio-DPA-redlines-v1.pdf (application/pdf, 512KB)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Keller <samantha.keller@asterbio.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Mar 2028 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment: credential model & operator access (DPA questions)

Samantha —

Appreciate the detailed redlines. Short answers up front and then a proposed next step below.

1) Customer-controlled keys: for our Private deployment patterns we support customer-managed keys (BYOK) inside a customer HSM/KMS instance that you control. Redwood components that need to encrypt/decrypt never obtain persistent access to the CMK. We support remote attestation and wrapped keys so operator accounts cannot export raw key material.

2) Support / break-glass: we propose an ephemeral session model where support engineers can request a time-limited, auditable session brokered by the customer's KMS with scoped capabilities (telemetry only / trace access). The KMS issues short-lived tokens that permit a read-only diagnostics API but do not grant decryption. All sessions are recorded and require dual-approval for elevated actions.

3) Telemetry & transfers: operator-visible telemetry is limited to anonymized operational logs and aggregated metrics (CPU/GPU, request latencies, error traces). We can produce a redacted logs sample for your security team. No unredacted model inputs/outputs will leave the VPC in the transferless configuration.

4) Subprocessors: out of transparency we can provide a constrained subprocessor list for this engagement and contractually restrict onshore/offshore processing. Note: if you opt for our hosted console for monitoring, additional cloud providers are involved; for strictly transferless private deploy we can keep the control plane in-customer or in a dedicated region.

Next step: I attached a draft addendum (proposed-dpa-addendum.docx) with language for a "No-key operator attestation" clause, limited subprocessor commitments, and a support-session protocol. Laura — can legal and security review the wording and advise edits? Samantha — I can host a call on Thursday 3/15 10:30AM PT if that works.

Best,

Aditya Rao
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai

Attachments: proposed-dpa-addendum.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document, 26KB)

Date: Wed, 14 Mar 2028 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment: credential model & operator access (DPA questions)

Samantha / Aditya —

Thanks for the context. A few legal/security clarifications I'll put on the table that should make procurement comfortable: 

- Subprocessor carveout: we can provide a fixed list of subprocessors for the transferless private deployment. That list will be contractually bound and limited to named entities (e.g., our dedicated colo partner and our telemetry aggregator in the US). No additional subprocessors will be added without 30 days' notice and written consent.

- Data transfers & residency: clause we propose: "No unredacted customer content will be exported from the customer's VPC or on-prem environment by Redwood or its subprocessors. Aggregated telemetry and health metrics may be transmitted for monitoring under the conditions described in Schedule X."

- Evidence and audit: we will provide SOC2 Type II attestation (redacted) and an operational runbook excerpt showing the ephemeral support flow. For legal signoff we can offer a limited right to audit (on-site/remote) with pre-approved scope and redaction for customer-sensitive content.

- Proposed clause language: I've added wording for a "credential separation" paragraph to the addendum and a recommended definition for "transferless deployment" (attached as tracked changes in the addendum). Please review and confirm whether the scope of logs we send (redacted) satisfies your reviewers.

Monica — can you pull the current subprocessor list for the dedicated private deployments and highlight which are US-only? Samantha — if AsterBio has any geographic constraints, flag them here and we'll mark the addendum accordingly.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai
